wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the task protects one resource, the read output of the entry itself; there is no neighbouring or proxy object whose authority could be checked instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: one operation (read or extract); there are no roles, peers or directions
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the only operation is the read; the sink is the read itself, and both the synchronous and asynchronous public read surfaces are covered
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: there is no identity or name parsing to malform; the guarded value is a numeric size field covered in its direct form
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no external authority, secret or role whose absence could fail open; the bound is computed locally
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the only adjacent API is the asynchronous read, which the functional suite drives directly through its callback contract

traps.shape: second implementation: the streaming inflater receives the same cap option object as the synchronous one but the streaming API ignores it, and it accumulates every emitted chunk without counting the total

traps.shape: a declared uncompressed size of exactly zero makes the cap condition false, so no output budget is passed at all; the same condition reads as a deliberate carve-out for empty entries
traps.realistic_because: the reported site in real, unmodified upstream code; a one-byte floor keeps genuinely empty entries readable while a rule that rejects size zero does not

traps.shape: trusted declared size: the same attacker-controlled uncompressed-size field sizes the output buffer before any data is read, so a tiny archive forces a multi-gigabyte allocation; large entries make the size look legitimate
